posts.name: Joseph Williams
posts.cooked:
Issue Statement:

We are attempting to import our companies historical data to migrate to ERPNext. As apart of that process, we are migrating current sales orders and historical sales orders. Currently, it appears that each unique address associated with a customer must be created separately and attached to the sales order. For us that would me creating thousands of addresses.

Issue Detailed Description:

Currently, in our ERP system, we can create a sales order that has a customer attached but no specific address object. Instead, we are able to create a “one-off” address that is linked to the sales order. This is often useful in many applications: for example, when a customer purchases an item from our web store as a guest, we would simply put the customer of the sales order as “GUEST” and create a one off address to record where to ship the item. This would not create an address object in relation to the customer, but instead a simple address associated with the sales order.

We are hoping to recreate that same flow into our ERPNext install. However, as of now, it appears we must create an address associated with the customer for each unique address we have and will ship to. This will leave us with thousands upon thousands of addresses associated with the “GUEST” customer account and similar.

Is there a way around this that fits within ERPNEXT’s framework?

posts.name: volkswagner
posts.cooked: This is an interesting challenge. I think you’ll want to create custom field(s) for custom_ship_to address in Sales Invoice. You can create a single rich text field (simple but not great for validation) or unique fields for addr1, addr2, city, state, and zip.

posts.name: Peer
posts.cooked:
What’s really the difference between “For us that would me creating thousands of addresses.” and “create a “one-off” address that is linked to the [implied: thousands of] sales order.”?

To me it sounds like an over-inflated problem, purely conceptional, even hardly technical at all.

You need specific data to fulfill an order, and if these reside in 1, 2 or 3 tables, what difference does it make? They need to be created and linked one way or another in any case, and they also need to be stored somewhere and be available for bureaucratic audits, reports, and your own controlling and error checking for some time.

It might take some time to get the import script right when starting with this system, but once you got it, you’re done with this “issue”, aren’t you?

IIRC, in a script you can supply the address (using the normal field names of an address record and its type) with the sales order object’s data and it will automatically be turned into a linked address record.
Otherwise, just create the address record (Address line 1, Address line 2, postcode, city, etc. and it’s type first, then insert its .name into the link field for the address in the sales order you create after creating the address, and then commit (one commit for both). That’s not a big deal to build.

posts.name: Joseph Williams
posts.cooked:
Two seperate updates/responses:

One of the key issues we are trying to fix is not having 1000+ addresses assocaited with a customer account.

For example, a “RETAIL” customer account, which we use to record sales for guests ordering on our site without an account. If we are to add each address and associate it with the “RETAIL” customer, it would be a list of 1000+ records.

I have tried syncing it in a way where each address is simply made in the address table without being associated with the customer, however ERPNext seems to reject it at time of import, because the address is not associated with the customer.

Seems this is not possible then?

posts.name: Peer
posts.cooked:
In fact, the question should be turned around:

What really happens is that all these POS sales invoices to retail customers have the selling point (the “POS” indeed) as the delivery address (handing out the items to the anonymous person). So instead of attaching many “null”-addresses to every SINV, there could be just one address, the one of the POS, put into all these SINVs. So just one address is needed for all SINVs of a given POS. Also, the customer could just be a unified (and somewhat hypothetical, having many identities) “anonymous walk-in customer”.
